blocks.text: The opening of the new Sirhind sequence explains why the city has become a moral target as well as a military one. The Singhs remember that innocent infants had been beheaded here, and that the city's name remains bound to the murder of the Guru's young sons and the oppression associated with their killers.
That memory transforms vengeance into collective policy. Sirhind is not merely to be raided but to be humbled, broken, and symbolically undone so that its punishment answers a long-carried grievance.

The page therefore frames the coming destruction as deliberate historical reckoning. What follows will be narrated not as random looting, but as the execution of justice remembered across generations.
